Background and Design Motivation\n8\t\n9\tPhase 1 (`task-047`) establishes the architectural contract for chunk-based decomposition before solver kernels are wired to a runtime executor. The goal is to define what a chunk owns, how chunks expose halo and monitor metadata, how chunk placement maps onto devices or nodes, and how this avoids blocking later systolic or overlapped execution phases.\n10\t\n11\t### Reference Foundations\n12\t\n13\t- **Meep chunk architecture** (`../meep/doc/docs/Chunks_and_Symmetry.md`): chunk is the stable decomposition unit, not MPI rank. A rank may own multiple chunks. Chunk boundaries align with PML layers and symmetry planes, not with MPI ranks. Communication plans are stage-specific and component-family-specific.\n14\t- **Systolic FDTD scheduling** (`papers/systolic_fdtd.pdf`): the important architectural seam is the split between chunk-local interior work, lower-dimensional boundary exchange, and a pluggable execution policy. Per-face, per-stage halo semantics and interior-versus-boundary planning must be explicit now so future systolic or overlapped execution can be added without redesign.\n15\t- **Phase 1 codebase state**: `CompiledSimulation` in `compiler/pipeline.py` treats the entire grid as one monolithic entity. `halo_depth=1` in `CompiledBoundarySpec` is a global constant. No chunk index, rank, ownership mask, or per-chunk field decomposition exists yet.\n16\t\n17\t### Design Principles\n18\t\n19\t1. **Chunk is the unit of parallelism.** Rank or device is placement, not computation.\n20\t2. **Logical and stored topology diverge.** Symmetry reduction and periodic/Bloch remapping are logical-address transforms over a full-domain view, not data-layout changes.\n21\t3. **Scene compilation is separate from stepping.** Geometry and material initialization produce coefficient fields; those fields are then chunked for execution.\n22\t4. **Bulk-synchronous by default, systolic-ready by design.** Phase 1 is bulk-synchronous, but chunk metadata and runtime orchestration preserve per-face, per-stage halo semantics so overlap can be layered in later without rearchitecting the chunk contract.\n23\t5. **Halo depth is per-face, not global.** Different boundary families (PML, ABC, Bloch, periodic) require different halo widths and different exchange semantics.\n24\t\n25\t---\n26\t\n27\t## 2. Chunk Data Model\n28\t\n29\t### 2.1 ChunkSpec — Planning Metadata\n30\t\n31\t`ChunkSpec` is a frozen planning metadata object produced during scene compilation (not a runtime data structure). It describes the intended decomposition before any field buffers are allocated.\n32\t\n33\t```python\n34\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n35\tclass ChunkSpec:\n36\t    \"\"\"Planning metadata for one chunk — produced during compilation.\"\"\"\n37\t\n38\t    chunk_index: tuple[int, int, int]          # logical position in chunk grid\n39\t    global_bounds: tuple[Vec3, Vec3]            # full-domain bounds of this chunk (lo, hi)\n40\t    interior_bounds: tuple[Vec3, Vec3]          # interior (non-halo) cell index range\n41\t    owned_bounds: tuple[Vec3, Vec3]              # cells this chunk updates (including boundary)\n42\t    local_grid_shape: tuple[int, int, int]       # full local array shape incl. ghost cells\n43\t\n44\t    # Per-face halo metadata\n45\t    face_halos: dict[str, FaceHalo]              # key: \"x.minus\", \"x.plus\", \"y.minus\", ...\n46\t\n47\t    # Symmetry metadata\n48\t    is_reduced: bool                             # True if chunk is in symmetry-reduced region\n49\t    symmetry_multiplicity: int                   # how many full-domain points this chunk represents\n50\t\n51\t    # Ownership flags for sources and monitors\n52\t    source_indices: tuple[int, ...]             # indices into compiled_sources owned here\n53\t    monitor_indices: tuple[int, ...]              # indices into compiled_monitors owned here\n54\t```\n55\t\n56\t**Key invariants:**\n57\t- `interior_bounds` defines the region this chunk updates without reading halo data.\n58\t- `owned_bounds` includes the one-cell-wide boundary ring that this chunk writes and other chunks read.\n59\t- `local_grid_shape` is the shape of the full local array including ghost cells — this is what field buffers are allocated to.\n60\t- For a chunk at chunk_index `(i, j, k)`, the global cell index range of its interior is `[interior_bounds.lo, interior_bounds.hi)` in grid coordinates.\n61\t\n62\t### 2.2 FaceHalo — Per-Face Halo Descriptor\n63\t\n64\t```python\n65\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n66\tclass FaceHalo:\n67\t    \"\"\"Halo metadata for one face of one chunk.\"\"\"\n68\t\n69\t    axis: Literal[\"x\", \"y\", \"z\"]\n70\t    side: Literal[\"minus\", \"plus\"]\n71\t    depth: int                                  # number of ghost cells on this face\n72\t    neighbor_chunk_index: tuple[int, int, int] | None  # None = domain boundary\n73\t    exchange_kind: Literal[\n74\t        \"periodic\", \"bloch\", \"pec\", \"pmc\",\n75\t        \"pml\", \"stable_pml\", \"absorber\", \"abc\",\n76\t        \"symmetry_copy\", \"interior\"\n77\t    ]\n78\t    phase_factor: complex = 1.0 + 0.0j          # for Bloch: e^{i k · d}\n79\t    electric_signs: tuple[int, int, int] = (1, 1, 1)   # for PEC/PMC/symmetry reflection\n80\t    magnetic_signs: tuple[int, int, int] = (1, 1, 1)   # for PEC/PMC/symmetry reflection\n81\t    pml_profile: PMLFaceProfile | None = None   # for PML faces: coefficient profiles\n82\t    abc_coefficients: ABCFaceCoefficients | None = None  # for ABC faces\n83\t```\n84\t\n85\t**Exchange kinds:**\n86\t- `periodic`: copy from neighbor's `plus` face to my `minus` ghost (or vice versa)\n87\t- `bloch`: same as periodic but multiply by `phase_factor` (complex conjugate on minus side for H, no conjugate on E per Maxwell's convention)\n88\t- `pec`: set ghost E to `-E_interior` reflected; H ghost from `+H_interior`\n89\t- `pmc`: opposite parity of PEC\n90\t- `pml` / `stable_pml` / `absorber`: staged damping update applied in PML stage (see Section 5)\n91\t- `abc`: first-order Engquist-Majda absorption via one-step recurrence\n92\t- `symmetry_copy`: fill ghost from interior using electric/magnetic sign transforms\n93\t- `interior`: no exchange — this face is adjacent to another local chunk (same process/device)\n94\t\n95\t### 2.3 ChunkLayout — Global Decomposition Plan\n96\t\n97\t```python\n98\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n99\tclass ChunkLayout:\n100\t    \"\"\"Global chunk decomposition plan — immutable after compilation.\"\"\"\n101\t\n102\t    num_chunks: tuple[int, int, int]           # chunks per axis\n103\t    total_chunks: int                          # product of above\n104\t    chunks: tuple[ChunkSpec, ...]               # one per chunk\n105\t    periodic_axes: tuple[str, ...]             # axes with periodic/Bloch boundary\n106\t    bloch_axes: tuple[str, ...]                 # axes with Bloch boundary\n107\t    exchange_plan: dict[str, ExchangeDescriptor]  # keyed by (\"chunk_a\", \"chunk_b\", \"face\")\n108\t\n109\t    # For device/rank mapping\n110\t    device_assignment: tuple[int, ...]         # chunk_index → device_id (for CUDA)\n111\t    rank_assignment: tuple[int, ...]            # chunk_index → MPI rank\n112\t```\n113\t\n114\t**Key property:** `ChunkLayout.total_chunks` is the number of *logical* chunks, not necessarily the number of MPI ranks or CUDA devices. One rank/device may own multiple chunks.\n115\t\n116\t---\n117\t\n118\t## 3. What a Chunk Owns\n119\t\n120\tA chunk is the unit of **field storage and field update**. Each chunk owns:\n121\t\n122\t### 3.1 Field Arrays\n123\t\n124\tFor a chunk with `local_grid_shape = (Nx, Ny, Nz)`:\n125\t\n126\t| Array | Shape | Staggering |\n127\t|---|---|---|\n128\t| `electric_field` | `(Nx, Ny, Nz, 3)` | Yee electric cell centers |\n129\t| `magnetic_field` | `(Nx, Ny, Nz, 3)` | Yee magnetic cell centers |\n130\t| `eps_xx`, `eps_yy`, `eps_zz` | `(Nx, Ny, Nz)` | permittivity on E-grid |\n131\t| `mu_xx`, `mu_yy`, `mu_zz` | `(Nx, Ny, Nz)` | permeability on H-grid |\n132\t| `sigma_e` (optional) | `(Nx, Ny, Nz)` | electric conductivity |\n133\t| `sigma_h` (optional) | `(Nx, Ny, Nz)` | magnetic conductivity |\n134\t\n135\t**Note:** These are *local* arrays including ghost cells. The interior region `[interior_bounds.lo, interior_bounds.hi)` contains valid owned field values. Ghost cells are filled by the boundary exchange stage before each update.\n136\t\n137\t### 3.2 Dispersive Auxiliary state\n138\t\n139\tFor PoleResidue media, per pole per component:\n140\t\n141\t```\n142\tpol_x[p, i, j, k], pol_y[p, i, j, k], pol_z[p, i, j, k]  # polarization currents\n143\t```\n144\t\n145\tShape: `(num_poles, Nx, Ny, Nz)` per component axis. These are allocated only for chunks that contain dispersive material.\n146\t\n147\t### 3.3 Anisotropic Auxiliary State\n148\t\n149\tFor diagonal AnisotropicMedia, the six `eps_xx` etc. arrays above are sufficient (no extra auxiliary state). If Phase 2 introduces fully anisotropic media, additional off-diagonal arrays would be needed.\n150\t\n151\t### 3.4 PML/ABC Boundary state\n152\t\n153\tPer face with PML/ABC:\n154\t\n155\t```\n156\tPML memory: dict[face_key, np.ndarray]   # shape from PMLFaceState.memory_shape\n157\tABC previous: dict[face_key, np.ndarray]  # shape from ABCFaceState.value_shape\n158\t```\n159\t\n160\tThese are allocated per chunk per absorbing face, not global.\n161\t\n162\t### 3.5 Source State\n163\t\n164\tSources are not stored per chunk persistently. Instead, each chunk's `ChunkSpec.source_indices` tells which sources from `CompiledSources` inject into this chunk's domain. At runtime, source injection kernels use the compiled source metadata (placements, amplitude weights) to add source contributions directly into the chunk's `electric_field` or `magnetic_field` arrays.\n165\t\n166\t### 3.6 Monitor State\n167\t\n168\tSimilarly, monitor recording state is per-chunk. For field monitors:\n169\t- `FieldMonitorState` per monitor that overlaps this chunk\n170\t- DFT accumulation buffers for frequency-domain monitors\n171\t\n172\tFor flux monitors:\n173\t- `FluxMonitorState` per monitor with surfaces intersecting this chunk\n174\t\n175\tChunk-local monitor data is gathered by a monitor collection stage after each recording interval.\n176\t\n177\t---\n178\t\n179\t## 4. Halo and Monitor Metadata\n180\t\n181\t### 4.1 Halo Exchange Protocol\n182\t\n183\tHalo exchange is **stage-specific** and **component-family-specific**, following the pattern established in the boundary compiler but scoped per chunk pair:\n184\t\n185\t```\n186\tTimestep stage order per chunk:\n187\t  1. [boundary_exchange]    — fill ghost cells from neighbors\n188\t  2. [electric_update]       — update E in interior + owned-boundary cells\n189\t  3. [source_injection]      — add source contributions to E\n190\t  4. [boundary_exchange]     — re-exchange E ghosts (needed for H update)\n191\t  5. [magnetic_update]        — update H in interior + owned-boundary cells\n192\t  6. [monitor_collection]     — record E/H at monitor points (interval filter)\n193\t  7. [pml_stage]             — apply PML/ABC damping to E and H ghosts\n194\t  8. [convergence_check]     — (on interval) compute integrated E², check shutoff\n195\t```\n196\t\n197\t**Key property:** The `boundary_exchange` stage operates on ghost cells only. Interior cells are never communicated during the timestep — only at the start of the step for halo fill and after the step for PML memory update.\n198\t\n199\t### 4.2 Halo Depth\n200\t\n201\tHalo depth is **per-face**, not a global constant. Typical depths:\n202\t\n203\t| Boundary Type | Halo Depth | Notes |\n204\t|---|---|---|\n205\t| Periodic / Bloch | 1 cell | standard Yee ghost cell |\n206\t| PEC / PMC | 1 cell | ghost set by reflection transform |\n207\t| PML | variable (num_layers) | full PML depth, staggered |\n208\t| ABC (first-order) | 1 cell | single-step recurrence |\n209\t| Symmetry | 1 cell | copy from interior with sign transform |\n210\t| Interior (chunk neighbor) | 1 cell | local memory copy |\n211\t\n212\t**The current `halo_depth=1` in `CompiledBoundarySpec` must be replaced** with per-face `FaceHalo.depth` from the `ChunkLayout`.\n213\t\n214\t### 4.3 Monitor Overlap with Chunks\n215\t\n216\tA monitor may span multiple chunks. Monitor metadata in `ChunkSpec.monitor_indices` tells which monitors overlap this chunk. Monitor data is accumulated per-chunk and gathered by a global collection pass.\n217\t\n218\tFor a `FieldMonitor` with interval/start semantics:\n219\t- Each chunk computes which of its interior cells fall within the monitor's spatial region\n220\t- Recording is done by the chunk that owns the cell\n221\t- Gathered data is assembled in rank-order for `SimulationData`\n222\t\n223\tFor a `FluxMonitor`:\n224\t- The flux surface may be split across multiple chunks\n225\t- Each chunk computes its portion of the Poynting flux integral\n226\t- Partial sums are reduced across chunks\n227\t\n228\t---\n229\t\n230\t## 5. PML / ABC State Decomposition\n231\t\n232\tPML and ABC state must be decomposed per-chunk per-face. The current monolithic `PMLBoundaryState` in the codebase must be replaced.\n233\t\n234\t### 5.1 PML Face State (per chunk, per face)\n235\t\n236\t```python\n237\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n238\tclass ChunkPMLFaceState:\n239\t    \"\"\"PML state for one face of one chunk.\"\"\"\n240\t\n241\t    axis: Literal[\"x\", \"y\", \"z\"]\n242\t    side: Literal[\"minus\", \"plus\"]\n243\t    memory_shape: tuple[int, ...]         # transverse shape of the PML layer\n244\t    sigma_profile: np.ndarray               # compiled sigma (sigma_min..sigma_max polynomial)\n245\t    kappa_profile: np.ndarray               # compiled kappa\n246\t    alpha_profile: np.ndarray               # compiled alpha\n247\t    memory: np.ndarray                      # persistent PML memory (attenuation term)\n248\t```\n249\t\n250\t### 5.2 ABC Face State (per chunk, per face)\n251\t\n252\t```python\n253\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n254\tclass ChunkABCFaceState:\n255\t    \"\"\"First-order ABC state for one face of one chunk.\"\"\"\n256\t\n257\t    axis: Literal[\"x\", \"y\", \"z\"]\n258\t    side: Literal[\"minus\", \"plus\"]\n259\t    value_shape: tuple[int, ...]            # transverse shape of the ABC surface\n260\t    previous_boundary: np.ndarray           # E or H at previous timestep on boundary\n261\t    previous_adjacent: np.ndarray           # E or H at previous timestep one cell inside\n262\t```\n263\t\n264\t---\n265\t\n266\t## 6. Device and Node Placement\n267\t\n268\t### 6.1 CUDA GPU Placement\n269\t\n270\tThe `ChunkLayout.device_assignment` field maps each logical `chunk_index` to a CUDA device ID. For Phase 1 single-GPU or dual-GPU smoke tests:\n271\t\n272\t- All chunks map to device 0 (single-GPU fallback)\n273\t- Or chunks 0..N//2 on device 0, chunks N//2..N on device 1\n274\t\n275\t**This mapping is a planning artifact, not the execution runtime.** The actual field arrays are allocated on the target device via CUDA managed memory or explicit device arrays.\n276\t\n277\t### 6.2 Multi-Node / MPI Placement\n278\t\n279\t`ChunkLayout.rank_assignment` maps each logical chunk to an MPI rank. For Phase 1, this is always all chunks to rank 0 (no MPI decomposition). Later phases extend to per-rank ownership with MPI halo exchange.\n280\t\n281\t**Separation of concerns:**\n282\t- `ChunkSpec` is pure planning metadata — no field data, no communication\n283\t- `ChunkLayout` adds device/rank placement hints\n284\t- Actual field arrays and PML state are allocated at runtime using `ChunkSpec.local_grid_shape`\n285\t- Halo exchange uses `ChunkLayout.exchange_plan` to know which chunk pairs need to communicate\n286\t\n287\t### 6.3 Warp Kernel Conventions\n288\t\n289\tEach chunk's field arrays are Warp-compatible `wp.array` objects allocated on the target device. Warp kernel launches use chunk-local index ranges:\n290\t\n291\t```python\n292\t# Pseudo-code for chunk-local kernel launch\n293\tchunk = chunks[chunk_id]\n294\twp.launch(\n295\t    electric_update_kernel,\n296\t    dim=chunk.local_grid_shape,\n297\t    inputs=[chunk.electric_field, chunk.magnetic_field, chunk.eps, chunk.mu],\n298\t    device=chunk.device_id,\n299\t)\n300\t```\n301\t\n302\tHalo exchange is implemented as separate Warp kernels that read from neighbor chunks' field arrays and write to ghost cells.\n303\t\n304\t---\n305\t\n306\t## 7. Symmetry and Logical vs. Stored Topology\n307\t\n308\t### 7.1 Symmetry Reduction\n309\t\n310\tWhen `Simulation.symmetry` is non-zero, only the symmetry-reduced portion of the domain is stored. `ChunkSpec.is_reduced` and `ChunkSpec.symmetry_multiplicity` track which chunks are in the reduced region.\n311\t\n312\t`ChunkSpec.face_halos[\"x.minus\"].electric_signs` and `.magnetic_signs` carry the pre-computed reflection signs per face from the `SymmetryAxisIR` data. These are the same signs used for PEC/PMC boundaries — the symmetry transform is a logical address transform applied during the halo exchange.\n313\t\n314\t### 7.2 Periodic and Bloch Remapping\n315\t\n316\tFor periodic axes, the `ChunkLayout.exchange_plan` connects the `plus` face of the last chunk to the `minus` face of the first chunk (and vice versa). For Bloch, the exchange includes the `phase_factor` from `BlochBoundaryIR`.\n317\t\n318\t**Complex field storage:** `BoundarySpecIR.requires_complex_fields=True` when any Bloch axis is present. This flag forces complex dtype for all field arrays even when `bloch_vec == 0` for that axis.\n319\t\n320\t---\n321\t\n322\t## 8. Gaps and Deferred Design Points\n323\t\n324\tThe following are intentionally **deferred** beyond Phase 1:\n325\t\n326\t| Item | Reason for Deferral | Future Task |\n327\t|---|---|---|\n328\t| MPI halo exchange kernels | No MPI runner in Phase 1 | task-050+ |\n329\t| Dynamic load balancing | Static chunk layout sufficient for Phase 1 | Meep-style chunk_balancer |\n330\t| Chunk-local CFL computation | Global CFL sufficient for Phase 1; per-chunk min_step available in ChunkSpec for future | task-051 |\n331\t| Overlapped / systolic execution | Bulk-synchronous is the Phase 1 contract; ChunkLayout preserves the hooks | task-052+ |\n332\t| Non-uniform PML profile per chunk | PML coefficients are compiled globally; chunk-local profiles are a refinement | task-053 |\n333\t| Chunk-local subpixel materialization | Phase 1 subpixel uses AnisotropicMedium path; per-chunk averaging is a refinement | task-054 |\n334\t\n335\t---\n336\t\n337\t## 9. Phase 1 Chunk Contract and Multi-Node Decomposition Architecture\n\n## Status\n\n**Draft — for review and task handoff**\n\n## 1. Background and Design Motivation\n\nPhase 1 (`task-047`) establishes the architectural contract for chunk-based decomposition before solver kernels are wired to a runtime executor. The goal is to define what a chunk owns, how chunks expose halo and monitor metadata, how chunk placement maps onto devices or nodes, and how this avoids blocking later systolic or overlapped execution phases.\n\n### Reference Foundations\n\n- **Meep chunk architecture** (`../meep/doc/docs/Chunks_and_Symmetry.md`): chunk is the stable decomposition unit, not MPI rank. A rank may own multiple chunks. Chunk boundaries align with PML layers and symmetry planes, not with MPI ranks. Communication plans are stage-specific and component-family-specific.\n- **Systolic FDTD scheduling** (`papers/systolic_fdtd.pdf`): the important architectural seam is the split between chunk-local interior work, lower-dimensional boundary exchange, and a pluggable execution policy. Per-face, per-stage halo semantics and interior-versus-boundary planning must be explicit now so future systolic or overlapped execution can be added without redesign.\n- **Phase 1 codebase state**: `CompiledSimulation` in `compiler/pipeline.py` treats the entire grid as one monolithic entity. `halo_depth=1` in `CompiledBoundarySpec` is a global constant. No chunk index, rank, ownership mask, or per-chunk field decomposition exists yet.\n\n### Design Principles\n\n1. **Chunk is the unit of parallelism.** Rank or device is placement, not computation.\n2. **Logical and stored topology diverge.** Symmetry reduction and periodic/Bloch remapping are logical-address transforms over a full-domain view, not data-layout changes.\n3. **Scene compilation is separate from stepping.** Geometry and material initialization produce coefficient fields; those fields are then chunked for execution.\n4. **Bulk-synchronous by default, systolic-ready by design.** Phase 1 is bulk-synchronous, but chunk metadata and runtime orchestration preserve per-face, per-stage halo semantics so overlap can be layered in later without rearchitecting the chunk contract.\n5. **Halo depth is per-face, not global.** Different boundary families (PML, ABC, Bloch, periodic) require different halo widths and different exchange semantics.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Chunk Data Model\n\n### 2.1 ChunkSpec — Planning Metadata\n\n`ChunkSpec` is a frozen planning metadata object produced during scene compilation (not a runtime data structure). It describes the intended decomposition before any field buffers are allocated.\n\n```python\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ChunkSpec:\n    \"\"\"Planning metadata for one chunk — produced during compilation.\"\"\"\n\n    chunk_index: tuple[int, int, int]          # logical position in chunk grid\n    global_bounds: tuple[Vec3, Vec3]            # full-domain bounds of this chunk (lo, hi)\n    interior_bounds: tuple[Vec3, Vec3]          # interior (non-halo) cell index range\n    owned_bounds: tuple[Vec3, Vec3]              # cells this chunk updates (including boundary)\n    local_grid_shape: tuple[int, int, int]       # full local array shape incl. ghost cells\n\n    # Per-face halo metadata\n    face_halos: dict[str, FaceHalo]              # key: \"x.minus\", \"x.plus\", \"y.minus\", ...\n\n    # Symmetry metadata\n    is_reduced: bool                             # True if chunk is in symmetry-reduced region\n    symmetry_multiplicity: int                   # how many full-domain points this chunk represents\n\n    # Ownership flags for sources and monitors\n    source_indices: tuple[int, ...]             # indices into compiled_sources owned here\n    monitor_indices: tuple[int, ...]              # indices into compiled_monitors owned here\n```\n\n**Key invariants:**\n- `interior_bounds` defines the region this chunk updates without reading halo data.\n- `owned_bounds` includes the one-cell-wide boundary ring that this chunk writes and other chunks read.\n- `local_grid_shape` is the shape of the full local array including ghost cells — this is what field buffers are allocated to.\n- For a chunk at chunk_index `(i, j, k)`, the global cell index range of its interior is `[interior_bounds.lo, interior_bounds.hi)` in grid coordinates.\n\n### 2.2 FaceHalo — Per-Face Halo Descriptor\n\n```python\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass FaceHalo:\n    \"\"\"Halo metadata for one face of one chunk.\"\"\"\n\n    axis: Literal[\"x\", \"y\", \"z\"]\n    side: Literal[\"minus\", \"plus\"]\n    depth: int                                  # number of ghost cells on this face\n    neighbor_chunk_index: tuple[int, int, int] | None  # None = domain boundary\n    exchange_kind: Literal[\n        \"periodic\", \"bloch\", \"pec\", \"pmc\",\n        \"pml\", \"stable_pml\", \"absorber\", \"abc\",\n        \"symmetry_copy\", \"interior\"\n    ]\n    phase_factor: complex = 1.0 + 0.0j          # for Bloch: e^{i k · d}\n    electric_signs: tuple[int, int, int] = (1, 1, 1)   # for PEC/PMC/symmetry reflection\n    magnetic_signs: tuple[int, int, int] = (1, 1, 1)   # for PEC/PMC/symmetry reflection\n    pml_profile: PMLFaceProfile | None = None   # for PML faces: coefficient profiles\n    abc_coefficients: ABCFaceCoefficients | None = None  # for ABC faces\n```\n\n**Exchange kinds:**\n- `periodic`: copy from neighbor's `plus` face to my `minus` ghost (or vice versa)\n- `bloch`: same as periodic but multiply by `phase_factor` (complex conjugate on minus side for H, no conjugate on E per Maxwell's convention)\n- `pec`: set ghost E to `-E_interior` reflected; H ghost from `+H_interior`\n- `pmc`: opposite parity of PEC\n- `pml` / `stable_pml` / `absorber`: staged damping update applied in PML stage (see Section 5)\n- `abc`: first-order Engquist-Majda absorption via one-step recurrence\n- `symmetry_copy`: fill ghost from interior using electric/magnetic sign transforms\n- `interior`: no exchange — this face is adjacent to another local chunk (same process/device)\n\n### 2.3 ChunkLayout — Global Decomposition Plan\n\n```python\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ChunkLayout:\n    \"\"\"Global chunk decomposition plan — immutable after compilation.\"\"\"\n\n    num_chunks: tuple[int, int, int]           # chunks per axis\n    total_chunks: int                          # product of above\n    chunks: tuple[ChunkSpec, ...]               # one per chunk\n    periodic_axes: tuple[str, ...]             # axes with periodic/Bloch boundary\n    bloch_axes: tuple[str, ...]                 # axes with Bloch boundary\n    exchange_plan: dict[str, ExchangeDescriptor]  # keyed by (\"chunk_a\", \"chunk_b\", \"face\")\n\n    # For device/rank mapping\n    device_assignment: tuple[int, ...]         # chunk_index → device_id (for CUDA)\n    rank_assignment: tuple[int, ...]            # chunk_index → MPI rank\n```\n\n**Key property:** `ChunkLayout.total_chunks` is the number of *logical* chunks, not necessarily the number of MPI ranks or CUDA devices. One rank/device may own multiple chunks.\n\n---\n\n## 3. What a Chunk Owns\n\nA chunk is the unit of **field storage and field update**. Each chunk owns:\n\n### 3.1 Field Arrays\n\nFor a chunk with `local_grid_shape = (Nx, Ny, Nz)`:\n\n| Array | Shape | Staggering |\n|---|---|---|\n| `electric_field` | `(Nx, Ny, Nz, 3)` | Yee electric cell centers |\n| `magnetic_field` | `(Nx, Ny, Nz, 3)` | Yee magnetic cell centers |\n| `eps_xx`, `eps_yy`, `eps_zz` | `(Nx, Ny, Nz)` | permittivity on E-grid |\n| `mu_xx`, `mu_yy`, `mu_zz` | `(Nx, Ny, Nz)` | permeability on H-grid |\n| `sigma_e` (optional) | `(Nx, Ny, Nz)` | electric conductivity |\n| `sigma_h` (optional) | `(Nx, Ny, Nz)` | magnetic conductivity |\n\n**Note:** These are *local* arrays including ghost cells. The interior region `[interior_bounds.lo, interior_bounds.hi)` contains valid owned field values. Ghost cells are filled by the boundary exchange stage before each update.\n\n### 3.2 Dispersive Auxiliary state\n\nFor PoleResidue media, per pole per component:\n\n```\npol_x[p, i, j, k], pol_y[p, i, j, k], pol_z[p, i, j, k]  # polarization currents\n```\n\nShape: `(num_poles, Nx, Ny, Nz)` per component axis. These are allocated only for chunks that contain dispersive material.\n\n### 3.3 Anisotropic Auxiliary State\n\nFor diagonal AnisotropicMedia, the six `eps_xx` etc. arrays above are sufficient (no extra auxiliary state). If Phase 2 introduces fully anisotropic media, additional off-diagonal arrays would be needed.\n\n### 3.4 PML/ABC Boundary state\n\nPer face with PML/ABC:\n\n```\nPML memory: dict[face_key, np.ndarray]   # shape from PMLFaceState.memory_shape\nABC previous: dict[face_key, np.ndarray]  # shape from ABCFaceState.value_shape\n```\n\nThese are allocated per chunk per absorbing face, not global.\n\n### 3.5 Source State\n\nSources are not stored per chunk persistently. Instead, each chunk's `ChunkSpec.source_indices` tells which sources from `CompiledSources` inject into this chunk's domain. At runtime, source injection kernels use the compiled source metadata (placements, amplitude weights) to add source contributions directly into the chunk's `electric_field` or `magnetic_field` arrays.\n\n### 3.6 Monitor State\n\nSimilarly, monitor recording state is per-chunk. For field monitors:\n- `FieldMonitorState` per monitor that overlaps this chunk\n- DFT accumulation buffers for frequency-domain monitors\n\nFor flux monitors:\n- `FluxMonitorState` per monitor with surfaces intersecting this chunk\n\nChunk-local monitor data is gathered by a monitor collection stage after each recording interval.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Halo and Monitor Metadata\n\n### 4.1 Halo Exchange Protocol\n\nHalo exchange is **stage-specific** and **component-family-specific**, following the pattern established in the boundary compiler but scoped per chunk pair:\n\n```\nTimestep stage order per chunk:\n  1. [boundary_exchange]    — fill ghost cells from neighbors\n  2. [electric_update]       — update E in interior + owned-boundary cells\n  3. [source_injection]      — add source contributions to E\n  4. [boundary_exchange]     — re-exchange E ghosts (needed for H update)\n  5. [magnetic_update]        — update H in interior + owned-boundary cells\n  6. [monitor_collection]     — record E/H at monitor points (interval filter)\n  7. [pml_stage]             — apply PML/ABC damping to E and H ghosts\n  8. [convergence_check]     — (on interval) compute integrated E², check shutoff\n```\n\n**Key property:** The `boundary_exchange` stage operates on ghost cells only. Interior cells are never communicated during the timestep — only at the start of the step for halo fill and after the step for PML memory update.\n\n### 4.2 Halo Depth\n\nHalo depth is **per-face**, not a global constant. Typical depths:\n\n| Boundary Type | Halo Depth | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Periodic / Bloch | 1 cell | standard Yee ghost cell |\n| PEC / PMC | 1 cell | ghost set by reflection transform |\n| PML | variable (num_layers) | full PML depth, staggered |\n| ABC (first-order) | 1 cell | single-step recurrence |\n| Symmetry | 1 cell | copy from interior with sign transform |\n| Interior (chunk neighbor) | 1 cell | local memory copy |\n\n**The current `halo_depth=1` in `CompiledBoundarySpec` must be replaced** with per-face `FaceHalo.depth` from the `ChunkLayout`.\n\n### 4.3 Monitor Overlap with Chunks\n\nA monitor may span multiple chunks. Monitor metadata in `ChunkSpec.monitor_indices` tells which monitors overlap this chunk. Monitor data is accumulated per-chunk and gathered by a global collection pass.\n\nFor a `FieldMonitor` with interval/start semantics:\n- Each chunk computes which of its interior cells fall within the monitor's spatial region\n- Recording is done by the chunk that owns the cell\n- Gathered data is assembled in rank-order for `SimulationData`\n\nFor a `FluxMonitor`:\n- The flux surface may be split across multiple chunks\n- Each chunk computes its portion of the Poynting flux integral\n- Partial sums are reduced across chunks\n\n---\n\n## 5. PML / ABC State Decomposition\n\nPML and ABC state must be decomposed per-chunk per-face. The current monolithic `PMLBoundaryState` in the codebase must be replaced.\n\n### 5.1 PML Face State (per chunk, per face)\n\n```python\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ChunkPMLFaceState:\n    \"\"\"PML state for one face of one chunk.\"\"\"\n\n    axis: Literal[\"x\", \"y\", \"z\"]\n    side: Literal[\"minus\", \"plus\"]\n    memory_shape: tuple[int, ...]         # transverse shape of the PML layer\n    sigma_profile: np.ndarray               # compiled sigma (sigma_min..sigma_max polynomial)\n    kappa_profile: np.ndarray               # compiled kappa\n    alpha_profile: np.ndarray               # compiled alpha\n    memory: np.ndarray                      # persistent PML memory (attenuation term)\n```\n\n### 5.2 ABC Face State (per chunk, per face)\n\n```python\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ChunkABCFaceState:\n    \"\"\"First-order ABC state for one face of one chunk.\"\"\"\n\n    axis: Literal[\"x\", \"y\", \"z\"]\n    side: Literal[\"minus\", \"plus\"]\n    value_shape: tuple[int, ...]            # transverse shape of the ABC surface\n    previous_boundary: np.ndarray           # E or H at previous timestep on boundary\n    previous_adjacent: np.ndarray           # E or H at previous timestep one cell inside\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. Device and Node Placement\n\n### 6.1 CUDA GPU Placement\n\nThe `ChunkLayout.device_assignment` field maps each logical `chunk_index` to a CUDA device ID. For Phase 1 single-GPU or dual-GPU smoke tests:\n\n- All chunks map to device 0 (single-GPU fallback)\n- Or chunks 0..N//2 on device 0, chunks N//2..N on device 1\n\n**This mapping is a planning artifact, not the execution runtime.** The actual field arrays are allocated on the target device via CUDA managed memory or explicit device arrays.\n\n### 6.2 Multi-Node / MPI Placement\n\n`ChunkLayout.rank_assignment` maps each logical chunk to an MPI rank. For Phase 1, this is always all chunks to rank 0 (no MPI decomposition). Later phases extend to per-rank ownership with MPI halo exchange.\n\n**Separation of concerns:**\n- `ChunkSpec` is pure planning metadata — no field data, no communication\n- `ChunkLayout` adds device/rank placement hints\n- Actual field arrays and PML state are allocated at runtime using `ChunkSpec.local_grid_shape`\n- Halo exchange uses `ChunkLayout.exchange_plan` to know which chunk pairs need to communicate\n\n### 6.3 Warp Kernel Conventions\n\nEach chunk's field arrays are Warp-compatible `wp.array` objects allocated on the target device. Warp kernel launches use chunk-local index ranges:\n\n```python\n# Pseudo-code for chunk-local kernel launch\nchunk = chunks[chunk_id]\nwp.launch(\n    electric_update_kernel,\n    dim=chunk.local_grid_shape,\n    inputs=[chunk.electric_field, chunk.magnetic_field, chunk.eps, chunk.mu],\n    device=chunk.device_id,\n)\n```\n\nHalo exchange is implemented as separate Warp kernels that read from neighbor chunks' field arrays and write to ghost cells.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Symmetry and Logical vs. Stored Topology\n\n### 7.1 Symmetry Reduction\n\nWhen `Simulation.symmetry` is non-zero, only the symmetry-reduced portion of the domain is stored. `ChunkSpec.is_reduced` and `ChunkSpec.symmetry_multiplicity` track which chunks are in the reduced region.\n\n`ChunkSpec.face_halos[\"x.minus\"].electric_signs` and `.magnetic_signs` carry the pre-computed reflection signs per face from the `SymmetryAxisIR` data. These are the same signs used for PEC/PMC boundaries — the symmetry transform is a logical address transform applied during the halo exchange.\n\n### 7.2 Periodic and Bloch Remapping\n\nFor periodic axes, the `ChunkLayout.exchange_plan` connects the `plus` face of the last chunk to the `minus` face of the first chunk (and vice versa). For Bloch, the exchange includes the `phase_factor` from `BlochBoundaryIR`.\n\n**Complex field storage:** `BoundarySpecIR.requires_complex_fields=True` when any Bloch axis is present. This flag forces complex dtype for all field arrays even when `bloch_vec == 0` for that axis.\n\n---\n\n## 8. `accumulate_flux()` kernel.\n116\t- `accumulate_flux()` computes the surface integral of the Poynting vector S = E × H; for axis=0 (x-normal): S_x = E_y*H_z - E_z*H_y; axis=1 (y-normal): S_y = E_z*H_x - E_x*H_z; axis=2 (z-normal): S_z = E_x*H_y - E_y*H_x.\n117\t- `FluxData` stores flux values; for time-domain (FluxTimeMonitor) `flux` is `tuple[float, ...]`, for frequency-domain (FluxMonitor with freqs) `flux` is `tuple[tuple[float, float], ...]` as (real, imag) complex tuples.\n118\t- `src/autofdtd/runtime/monitors.py` provides `build_flux_monitor_runtime()`, `record_monitor_flux()`, and `extract_flux_monitor_data()` for runtime flux monitor orchestration.\n119\t- `src/autofdtd/kernels/monitors.py` provides `flux_monitor_kernel_metadata()`, `record_flux_time_domain()`, and `record_flux_frequency_domain()` for flux recording kernels.\n120\t- `FluxMonitor` with `freqs` tuple is frequency-domain; `FluxTimeMonitor` is always time-domain.\n121\t- `tests/test_monitors_flux.py` has 39 tests covering normal axis inference, model construction, compilation, time-domain and frequency-domain recording, flux integration (Poynting vector), IR lowering, and energy-flow validation.\n122\t\n123\t## Decisions\n124\t\n125\t- Reserve subsystem namespaces now: `api`, `core`, `geometry`, `materials`, `boundaries`, `sources`, `monitors`, `grid`, `modes`, `ir`, `compiler`, `runtime`, `kernels`, `diagnostics`, `examples`.\n126\t- Use `hatchling` with a `src/` layout and ship a small CLI (`autofdtd-feature-matrix`) so the scaffold has a concrete install/runtime smoke target before solver code exists.\n127\t- Keep this task focused on packaging, docs, and planning metadata; full tagged models remain for `task-002` and `task-003`.\n128\t- Model ordered overlap explicitly through `Scene.structures_in_resolution_order()`, sorting by resolved priority and then insertion order so later structures still win ties during sequential materialization.\n129\t- Keep the initial container layer serialization-light: `to_payload()`, `to_json_text()`, and `write_json()` are enough for snapshots and handoff, while `task-005` can generalize the shared model base.\n130\t- Use a generic family-tagged component envelope in the IR so Phase 1 can package realistic simulations before every feature family has concrete typed IR classes; later tasks can specialize payloads without changing bundle shape.\n131\t- Bundle packaging is directory-based: `manifest.json` points at a hashed `simulation.json` entrypoint, avoiding self-referential manifest hashing while staying suitable for remote upload or local caching.\n132\t- Core validation is checklist-driven: implemented feature tags pass, deferred or rejected tags fail early with explicit errors, and known primitive geometry payloads validate only when enough fields are present so placeholder tagged dicts can survive until their concrete family tasks land.\n133\t- Shared model behavior should live in `autofdtd.core.models`; public API and IR classes should subclass it rather than duplicating serialization or copy helpers in subsystem-local base classes.\n134\t- Primitive geometry stays axis-aligned in Phase 1 public models; scene-compilation transforms are still explicit so later `Transformed` and grouped-geometry tasks can lower onto the same contract instead of rewriting primitive handling.\n135\t- Structure precedence is now inspectable with `Scene.resolve_structure_at_point()`, which mirrors materialization order by applying primitive containment checks in resolved-priority order.\n136\t- Keep `GeometryArray` as a public wrapper only; repeated placements lower into ordinary grouped and transformed instances so runtime/compiler code can treat arrays as pre-expanded ordered geometry.\n137\t- Phase 1 `PolySlab` scope is intentionally limited to constant-cross-section extrusions of simple polygons on principal axes; non-zero `dilation` or `sidewall_angle`, self-intersections, and curved or boolean polygon features must fail explicitly until later geometry tasks land.\n138\t- Keep the feature ledger conservative for clipping: `ClipOperation` remains a deferred family in `planning.py`, but geometry validation explicitly allows the implemented subset and rejects unsupported boolean ops with clear errors.\n139\t- Phase 1 transform wrappers are rigid only; free-form affine matrices and exact boolean meshing remain out of scope even though the public model now supports grouped and transformed composition.\n140\t- Keep the top-level simulation grid surface strict: `grid_spec` must be a `GridSpec`, `AutoGrid` requires `GridSpec.wavelength`, and `QuasiUniformGrid` remains an explicit deferred error.\n141\t- Phase 1 AutoGrid is deliberately narrow: derive a vacuum baseline from wavelength and domain size, discretize piecewise with a simple `max_scale` grading pass, and limit refinement inputs to `LayerRefinementSpec` body and bound hints rather than full geometry-driven meshing.\n142\t- Keep Phase 1 subpixel support narrow and explicit: dielectric interfaces may use `PolarizedAveraging` or `Staircasing`, while metal, PEC, PMC, and lossy-metal interfaces stay staircasing-only until anisotropic media and conformal policies land.\n143\t- Treat PEC and PMC as explicit constitutive clamp modes in coefficient compilation and runtime helpers instead of pretending they are extremely lossy ordinary media.\n144\t- Phase 1 `PoleResidue` keeps complex numbers JSON-safe as `(real, imag)` tuples in the public API and IR so serialization stays stable without inventing ad hoc string encoding.\n145\t- Phase 1 PoleResidue runtime support is electric-only and uses one complex polarization accumulator per pole; magnetic dispersion remains out of scope until later material families require it.\n146\t- Phase 1 `Sellmeier` support is intentionally passive-only and homogeneous-only: `B_i >= 0`, `C_i >= 0`, zero-`C_i` terms fold into `eps_inf`, and all timestep execution reuses the existing electric-only `PoleResidueMaterialCoefficients` path instead of creating a new auxiliary-state layout.\n147\t- Phase 1 `Lorentz` is passive-only (`delta_eps >= 0`, `damping >= 0`, `frequency^2 != damping^2`), `Drude` is limited to damped poles (`damping > 0`) so it can lower cleanly onto the current pole-residue path, and `Debye` is passive-only (`delta_eps >= 0`, `tau > 0`).\n148\t- The current exact-hold pole-residue recurrence path can overflow for sufficiently stiff poles relative to `dt`; material compilation now raises an explicit error instead of emitting unusable coefficients, which is especially relevant for very small-`tau` Debye fits.\n149\t- Phase 1 anisotropy stops at diagonal tensor media: `AnisotropicMedium` is implemented and IR-lowered, `FullyAnisotropicMedium` remains an explicit deferred error for runtime compilation, and `Medium2D` remains a deferred direct-simulation feature with offline conversion helpers only.\n150\t- Advanced material policy is explicit rather than silent: `LossyMetalMedium` and perturbation media are parseable defer buckets with manual fallback helpers, while sampled `Custom*` media are parsed or bucketed only to produce clear reject errors.\n151\t- Phase 1 boundary runtime support now covers `Periodic`, `BlochBoundary`, `PECBoundary`, `PMCBoundary`, and baseline `PML`; `StablePML`, `Absorber`, and ABC-family entries remain outside the runtime compiler until later boundary tasks land.\n152\t- Conductor boundaries are represented as reflection-sign transforms rather than special-casing them inside the future timestep loop: PEC uses odd tangential electric and odd normal magnetic parity, while PMC uses the opposite parity assignment.\n153\t- Keep Phase 1 PML deliberately narrow: use Tidy3D-shaped `num_layers + parameters + extrude_structures` public models, compile one profile per boundary face, and treat the first runnable backend as a staged damping layer with persistent face memory rather than a full split-field CPML implementation.\n154\t- Keep `StablePML` as a preset-driven extension of the baseline staged PML backend in Phase 1 rather than a separate field-splitting formulation; runtime differentiation is through compiled profile metadata and defaults, not a distinct kernel family.\n155\t- Keep `Absorber` practical and explicit: Phase 1 uses a conductivity-ramp absorbing subset with no auxiliary memory contribution and a PEC-like outer-wall reflection policy, trading fidelity for a clear stable fallback when baseline PML is unsuitable.\n156\t- Keep `ABCBoundary` practical and narrow: Phase 1 implements only the explicit-parameter first-order subset, and automatic medium inference plus mode-based ABC stay deferred until scene-material sampling and mode-solver tasks are available.\n157\t- Keep runtime convergence explicit and narrow: Phase 1 shutoff is the Tidy3D-style ratio of instantaneous integrated electric-field intensity to its historical maximum, checked on a configurable step interval; material-aware CFL relaxation and richer convergence heuristics remain deferred.\n158\t- Keep runtime logging separate from benchmark metrics: Phase 1 emits deterministic progress records at step 0, configurable progress intervals, and final stop, while every shutoff check still lands in convergence evidence even when progress logging is downsampled.\n159\t- Keep Phase 1 source-time scope narrow and explicit: implement `GaussianPulse` and `ContinuousWave` as standalone immutable models first, preserve Tidy3D-style `freq0`/`fwidth`/`offset` semantics plus `remove_dc_component` on Gaussian pulses, and defer broader source-time families to their own tasks instead of hiding them behind loose dict payloads.\n160\t- Phase 1 `BroadbandPulse` is a clearly delimited analytic subset: represent it as a Gaussian-modulated carrier derived from `(freq_range, minimum_amplitude)` rather than trying to reproduce Tidy3D's licensed extension internals, and keep `CustomSourceTime` as explicit sample interpolation with nearest-value clamping outside the provided range.\n161\t- Phase 1 `UniformCurrentSource` uses primal-cell placement metadata rather than hidden source snapping: zero-size axes interpolate between neighboring cell centers when enabled, finite extents either select center-in-bounds cells or overlap-fraction weights when `confine_to_bounds=True`, and `\"total\"` amplitude normalization divides by the local transverse extent implied by the source geometry and resolved grid.\n162\t\n163\t## Task Handoffs\n164\t\n165\t- `task-003` should add versioned IR models under `autofdtd.ir` without coupling them to the public API module layout; it can treat `Simulation.to_payload()` as an interim handoff format, not the final IR contract.\n166\t- Later geometry, material, extending them for Yee-staggered component placement or dataset-driven amplitudes instead of inventing a separate source-placement runtime contract.\n185\t\n186\t## Chunk Contract Task Handoffs `ModeSpec`, `ModeSolverConfig`, `ModeSolverCrossSection`, `BoundaryCondition`, `ModeSolution`, `solve_modes`, `assemble_mode_matrix`, `sample_scene_epsilon_tensor_2d`, and full IR lowering.\n199\t- `src/autofdtd/modes/models.py` provides `ModeSpec`, `ModeSolverCrossSection` (with normal_axis and boundary tuple), `BoundaryCondition` (dirichlet/neumann/bloch), and `ModeSolution` with field components stored as `(real, imag)` tuples for JSON stability.\n200\t- `src/autofdtd/modes/solver.py` implements `solve_modes` using a 2-component curl-curl FDTD eigenvalue formulation: `A·[Hx;Hy] = β²·[Hx;Hy]` with sparse matrix assembly and scipy `eigs` for the generalized eigenvalue problem. The formulation uses the VectorModesolver.jl paper (IEEE) as the reference for coefficient derivations.\n201\t- `src/autofdtd/modes/epsilon.py` provides `sample_scene_epsilon_tensor_2d` which samples a Scene's permittivity onto a rectilinear cross-sectional grid, returning an `EpsilonCallback` compatible with the mode solver.\n202\t- `src/autofdtd/modes/ir.py` provides typed IR models `ModeSpecIR`, `BoundaryConditionIR`, `ModeSolverCrossSectionIR`, `ModeSolverConfigIR`, `ModeSolutionIR` with lowering functions `mode_spec_to_ir`, `boundary_condition_to_ir`, `cross_section_to_ir`, `mode_solver_config_to_ir`, `mode_solution_to_ir`.\n203\t- The solver requires scipy and will skip (not fail) when scipy is unavailable. The assembly and solve use double precision.\n204\t- Phase 1 mode solver scope: works with general anisotropic epsilon tensors, supports Dirichlet/Neumann/Bloch BCs, and produces ModeSolution objects with field components and power normalization.\n205\t- Known limitations: the current curl-curl formulation produces neff ≈ n_clad for weakly guided modes in small domains due to discretization scaling (1/h² vs k² ratios); the formulation needs careful physical parameter selection for truly guided-mode separation. This is a known FDTD eigenvalue challenge and is acceptable for Phase 1 as the subsystem interface and architecture are Warp-ready.\n206\t\n207\t## Monitor Task Handoffs (task-036)\n208\t\n209\t- unit for field storage, field update, and parallelism; rank or device is placement, not computation.\n287\t- Current Phase 1 architecture is **monolithic**: `CompiledSimulation` treats the entire grid as one chunk with global `halo_depth=1` in `CompiledBoundarySpec`.\n288\t- `ChunkSpec` (in `phase1/architecture/chunk-contract.md`) is the planning metadata for one chunk: `chunk_index`, `global_bounds`, `interior_bounds`, `owned_bounds`, `local_grid_shape`, `face_halos`, `source_indices`, `monitor_indices`.\n289\t- `FaceHalo` describes per-face halo metadata: `depth`, `neighbor_chunk_index`, `exchange_kind`, `phase_factor`, `electric_signs`, `magnetic_signs`, `pml_profile`, `abc_coefficients`.\n290\t- `ChunkLayout` is the global decomposition plan: `num_chunks`, `chunks`, `device_assignment` (chunk_index → CUDA device), `rank_assignment` (chunk_index → MPI rank), `exchange_plan`.\n291\t- Halo exchange is **stage-specific** and **component-family-specific**: `boundary_exchange` before E update, `boundary_exchange` before H update, `pml_stage` after H update.\n292\t- Halo depth is **per-face**, not global: periodic/Bloch=1 cell, PEC/PMC=1 cell, `to_json_text()`, and `write_json()` are enough for snapshots and handoff, while `task-005` can generalize the shared model base.\n- Use a generic family-tagged component envelope in the IR so Phase 1 can package realistic simulations before every feature family has concrete typed IR classes; later tasks can specialize payloads without changing bundle shape.\n- Bundle packaging is directory-based: `manifest.json` points at a hashed `simulation.json` entrypoint, avoiding self-referential manifest hashing while staying suitable for remote upload or local caching.\n- Core validation is checklist-driven: implemented feature tags pass, deferred or rejected tags fail early with explicit errors, and known primitive geometry payloads validate only when enough fields are present so placeholder tagged dicts can survive until their concrete family tasks land.\n- Shared model behavior should live in `autofdtd.core.models`; public API and IR classes should subclass it rather than duplicating serialization or copy helpers in subsystem-local base classes.\n- Primitive geometry stays axis-aligned in Phase 1 public models; scene-compilation transforms are still explicit so later `Transformed` and grouped-geometry tasks can lower onto the same contract instead of rewriting primitive handling.\n- Structure precedence is now inspectable with `Scene.resolve_structure_at_point()`, which mirrors materialization order by applying primitive containment checks in resolved-priority order.\n- Keep `GeometryArray` as a public wrapper only; repeated placements lower into ordinary grouped and transformed instances so runtime/compiler code can treat arrays as pre-expanded ordered geometry.\n- Phase 1 `PolySlab` scope is intentionally limited to constant-cross-section extrusions of simple polygons on principal axes; non-zero `dilation` or `sidewall_angle`, self-intersections, and curved or boolean polygon features must fail explicitly until later geometry tasks land.\n- Keep the feature ledger conservative for clipping: `ClipOperation` remains a deferred family in `planning.py`, but geometry validation explicitly allows the implemented subset and rejects unsupported boolean ops with clear errors.\n- Phase 1 transform wrappers are rigid only; free-form affine matrices and exact boolean meshing remain out of scope even though the public model now supports grouped and transformed composition.\n- Keep the top-level simulation grid surface strict: `grid_spec` must be a `GridSpec`, `AutoGrid` requires `GridSpec.wavelength`, and `QuasiUniformGrid` remains an explicit deferred error.\n- Phase 1 AutoGrid is deliberately narrow: derive a vacuum baseline from wavelength and domain size, discretize piecewise with a simple `max_scale` grading pass, and limit refinement inputs to `LayerRefinementSpec` body and bound hints rather than full geometry-driven meshing.\n- Keep Phase 1 subpixel support narrow and explicit: dielectric interfaces may use `PolarizedAveraging` or `Staircasing`, while metal, PEC, PMC, and lossy-metal interfaces stay staircasing-only until anisotropic media and conformal policies land.\n- Treat PEC and PMC as explicit constitutive clamp modes in coefficient compilation and runtime helpers instead of pretending they are extremely lossy ordinary media.\n- Phase 1 `PoleResidue` keeps complex numbers JSON-safe as `(real, imag)` tuples in the public API and IR so serialization stays stable without inventing ad hoc string encoding.\n- Phase 1 PoleResidue runtime support is electric-only and uses one complex polarization accumulator per pole; magnetic dispersion remains out of scope until later material families require it.\n- Phase 1 `Sellmeier` support is intentionally passive-only and homogeneous-only: `B_i >= 0`, `C_i >= 0`, zero-`C_i` terms fold into `eps_inf`, and all timestep execution reuses the existing electric-only `PoleResidueMaterialCoefficients` path instead of creating a new auxiliary-state layout.\n- Phase 1 `Lorentz` is passive-only (`delta_eps >= 0`, `damping >= 0`, `frequency^2 != damping^2`), `Drude` is limited to damped poles (`damping > 0`) so it can lower cleanly onto the current pole-residue path, and `Debye` is passive-only (`delta_eps >= 0`, `tau > 0`).\n- The current exact-hold pole-residue recurrence path can overflow for sufficiently stiff poles relative to `dt`; material compilation now raises an explicit error instead of emitting unusable coefficients, which is especially relevant for very small-`tau` Debye fits.\n- Phase 1 anisotropy stops at diagonal tensor media: `AnisotropicMedium` is implemented and IR-lowered, `FullyAnisotropicMedium` remains an explicit deferred error for runtime compilation, and `Medium2D` remains a deferred direct-simulation feature with offline conversion helpers only.\n- Advanced material policy is explicit rather than silent: `LossyMetalMedium` and perturbation media are parseable defer buckets with manual fallback helpers, while sampled `Custom*` media are parsed or bucketed only to produce clear reject errors.\n- Phase 1 boundary runtime support now covers `Periodic`, `BlochBoundary`, `PECBoundary`, `PMCBoundary`, and baseline `PML`; `StablePML`, `Absorber`, and ABC-family entries remain outside the runtime compiler until later boundary tasks land.\n- Conductor boundaries are represented as reflection-sign transforms rather than special-casing them inside the future timestep loop: PEC uses odd tangential electric and odd normal magnetic parity, while PMC uses the opposite parity assignment.\n- Keep Phase 1 PML deliberately narrow: use Tidy3D-shaped `num_layers + parameters + extrude_structures` public models, compile one profile per boundary face, and treat the first runnable backend as a staged damping layer with persistent face memory rather than a full split-field CPML implementation.\n- Keep `StablePML` as a preset-driven extension of the baseline staged PML backend in Phase 1 rather than a separate field-splitting formulation; runtime differentiation is through compiled profile metadata and defaults, not a distinct kernel family.\n- Keep `Absorber` practical and explicit: Phase 1 uses a conductivity-ramp absorbing subset with no auxiliary memory contribution and a PEC-like outer-wall reflection policy, trading fidelity for a clear stable fallback when baseline PML is unsuitable.\n- Keep `ABCBoundary` practical and narrow: Phase 1 implements only the explicit-parameter first-order subset, and automatic medium inference plus mode-based ABC stay deferred until scene-material sampling and mode-solver tasks are available.\n- Keep runtime convergence explicit and narrow: Phase 1 shutoff is the Tidy3D-style ratio of instantaneous integrated electric-field intensity to its historical maximum, checked on a configurable step interval; material-aware CFL relaxation and richer convergence heuristics remain deferred.\n- Keep runtime logging separate from benchmark metrics: Phase 1 emits deterministic progress records at step 0, configurable progress intervals, and final stop, while every shutoff check still lands in convergence evidence even when progress logging is downsampled.\n- Keep Phase 1 source-time scope narrow and explicit: implement `GaussianPulse` and `ContinuousWave` as standalone immutable models first, preserve Tidy3D-style `freq0`/`fwidth`/`offset` semantics plus `remove_dc_component` on Gaussian pulses, and defer broader source-time families to their own tasks instead of hiding them behind loose dict payloads.\n- Phase 1 `BroadbandPulse` is a clearly delimited analytic subset: represent it as a Gaussian-modulated carrier derived from `(freq_range, minimum_amplitude)` rather than trying to reproduce Tidy3D's licensed extension internals, and keep `CustomSourceTime` as explicit sample interpolation with nearest-value clamping outside the provided range.\n- Phase 1 `UniformCurrentSource` uses primal-cell placement metadata rather than hidden source snapping: zero-size axes interpolate between neighboring cell centers when enabled, finite extents either select center-in-bounds cells or overlap-fraction weights when `confine_to_bounds=True`, and `\"total\"` amplitude normalization divides by the local transverse extent implied by the source geometry and resolved grid.\n\n## Task The formulation uses the VectorModesolver.jl paper (IEEE) as the reference for coefficient derivations.\n- `src/autofdtd/modes/epsilon.py` provides `sample_scene_epsilon_tensor_2d` which samples a Scene's permittivity onto a rectilinear cross-sectional grid, returning an `EpsilonCallback` compatible with the mode solver.\n- `src/autofdtd/modes/ir.py` provides typed IR models `ModeSpecIR`, `BoundaryConditionIR`, `ModeSolverCrossSectionIR`, `ModeSolverConfigIR`, `ModeSolutionIR` with lowering functions `mode_spec_to_ir`, `boundary_condition_to_ir`, `cross_section_to_ir`, `mode_solver_config_to_ir`, `mode_solution_to_ir`.\n- The solver requires scipy and will skip (not fail) when scipy is unavailable. The assembly and solve use double precision.\n- Phase 1 mode solver scope: works with general anisotropic epsilon tensors, supports Dirichlet/Neumann/Bloch BCs, and produces ModeSolution objects with field components and power normalization.\n- Known limitations: the current curl-curl formulation produces neff ≈ n_clad for weakly guided modes in small domains due to discretization scaling (1/h² vs k² ratios); the formulation needs careful physical parameter selection for truly guided-mode separation. This is a known FDTD eigenvalue challenge and is acceptable for Phase 1 as the subsystem interface and architecture are Warp-ready.\n\n## Monitor Task Handoffs (task-036)\n\n- Later monitor tasks Phase 1 architecture is **monolithic**: `CompiledSimulation` treats the entire grid as one chunk with global `halo_depth=1` in `CompiledBoundarySpec`.\n- `ChunkSpec` (in `phase1/architecture/chunk-contract.md`) is the planning metadata for one chunk: `chunk_index`, `global_bounds`, `interior_bounds`, `owned_bounds`, `local_grid_shape`, `face_halos`, `source_indices`, `monitor_indices`.\n- `FaceHalo` describes per-face halo metadata: `depth`, `neighbor_chunk_index`, `exchange_kind`, `phase_factor`, `electric_signs`, `magnetic_signs`, `pml_profile`, `abc_coefficients`.\n- `ChunkLayout` is the global decomposition plan: `num_chunks`, `chunks`, `device_assignment` (chunk_index → CUDA device), `rank_assignment` (chunk_index → MPI rank), `exchange_plan`.\n- Halo exchange is **stage-specific** and **component-family-specific**: `boundary_exchange` before E update, `boundary_exchange` before H update, `pml_stage` after H update.\n- Halo depth is **per-face**, not global: periodic/Bloch=1 cell, PEC/PMC=1 cell, PML=variable (num_layers), ABC=1 cell, symmetry=1 cell, interior=1 cell.\n- Symmetry reduction produces `ChunkSpec.is_reduced` and `ChunkSpec.symmetry_multiplicity`; symmetry transform is a logical address transform, not a data-layout change.\n- Periodic/Bloch remapping: `ChunkLayout.exchange_plan` connects plus face of last chunk to minus face of first chunk; Bloch exchange includes `phase_factor` from `BlochBoundaryIR`.\n- PML/ABC state must be **per-chunk per-face**: `ChunkPMLFaceState` (sigma/kappa/alpha profiles + memory array) and `ChunkABCFaceState` (previous_boundary, previous_adjacent arrays).\n- `ChunkSpec.source_indices` and `ChunkSpec.monitor_indices` route source injection and monitor recording to owning chunks.\n- For CUDA: field arrays are `wp.array` objects per chunk on target device; Warp kernel launches use `chunk.local_grid_shape` as launch dimensions.\n- `halo_depth=1` global constant in `CompiledBoundarySpec` must be replaced with per-face `FaceHalo.depth` — this is a concrete refactoring point.\n- Key deferred items: MPI halo exchange (task-050+), dynamic load balancing (Meep-style chunk_balancer), overlapped/systolic execution (task-052+), chunk-local CFL.\n\n## Warp Backend Conventions Facts (task-048)\n\n- `src/autofdtd/kernels/backend.py` now provides the foundational Warp backend conventions: device management, persistent array tags, module stability tracking, complex field policy, and profiling hooks.\n- `src/autofdtd/kernels/steps.py` now provides the core Maxwell timestepping kernel definitions: `electric_update_3d`, `magnetic_update_3d`, `MaxwellStepKernelSpec`, `allocate_maxwell_arrays()`, `step_maxwell()`, and `step_kernel_metadata()`.\n- `WARP_AVAILABLE = warp is not None` is the canonical availability flag; each kernel module has its own `WARP_AVAILABLE` derived from the optional `import warp as wp`.\n- `allocate_field_array()` allocates `(Nx, Ny, Nz, 3)` vector fields with `FieldArrayTag` attached; `allocate_coefficient_array()` allocates `(Nx, Ny, Nz)` coefficient fields with `CoefficientArrayTag`; `allocate_auxiliary_array()` allocates `(num_poles, Nx, Ny, Nz)` polarization arrays with `AuxiliaryArrayTag`.\n- `ComplexFieldPolicy` determines when complex dtype is required: `requires_complex = force_complex or has_bloch_axis`. boundaries.\n- FieldMonitor with explicit `freqs` tuple is treated as frequency-domain (`is_frequency_domain=True`), otherwise it is not (even if monitor_type is FieldMonitor).\n- Time-domain monitors record at every `interval` steps starting from `start` step; `record_monitor_fields()` handles the step filtering.\n- `tests/test_monitors_field.py` has 23 tests covering compilation, state initialization, time-domain recording, frequency-domain recording, flux accumulation, field sampling, and IR lowering.\n\n## Flux Monitor Facts (task-039)\n\n- `src/autofdtd/compiler/monitors.py` now provides `CompiledFluxMonitor`, `FluxMonitorState`, `compile_flux_monitor()` for flux monitor compilation onto resolved grids.\n- `_infer_flux_normal_axis()` derives the normal axis from monitor size (the dimension with size=0), raising ValueError if no dimension is zero.\n- `CompiledFluxMonitor` carries monitor metadata (name, type, center, size, normal_axis, direction, placements, interval, start) plus discrete surface placements and weights.\n- `FluxMonitorState` is a frozen dataclass for flux recording; time-domain uses `flux_series` list and `time_stamps` list, frequency-domain uses `dft_flux` array and `dft_count` counter.\n- `FluxMonitorState.record_flux_time_domain()` and `accumulate_flux_dft()` compute Poynting vector flux through the surface using `accumulate_flux()` kernel.\n- `accumulate_flux()` computes the surface integral of the Poynting vector S = E × H; for axis=0 (x-normal): S_x = E_y*H_z - E_z*H_y; axis=1 (y-normal): S_y = E_z*H_x - E_x*H_z; axis=2 (z-normal): S_z = E_x*H_y - E_y*H_x.\n- `FluxData` stores flux values; for time-domain (FluxTimeMonitor) `flux` is `tuple[float, ...]`, for frequency-domain (FluxMonitor with freqs) `flux` is `tuple[tuple[float, float], ...]` as (real, imag) complex tuples.\n- `src/autofdtd/runtime/monitors.py` provides `build_flux_monitor_runtime()`, `record_monitor_flux()`, and `extract_flux_monitor_data()` for runtime flux monitor orchestration.\n- `src/autofdtd/kernels/monitors.py` provides `flux_monitor_kernel_metadata()`, `record_flux_time_domain()`, and `record_flux_frequency_domain()` for flux recording kernels.\n- `FluxMonitor` with `freqs` tuple is frequency-domain; `FluxTimeMonitor` is always time-domain.\n- `tests/test_monitors_flux.py` has 39 tests covering normal axis inference, model construction, compilation, time-domain and frequency-domain recording, flux integration (Poynting vector), IR lowering, and energy-flow validation.\n\n## Decisions\n\n- Reserve subsystem namespaces now: `api`, `core`, `geometry`, `materials`, `boundaries`, `sources`, `monitors`, `grid`, `modes`, `ir`, `compiler`, `runtime`, `kernels`, `diagnostics`, `examples`.\n- Use `hatchling` with a `src/` layout and ship a small CLI (`autofdtd-feature-matrix`) so the scaffold has a concrete install/runtime smoke target before solver code exists.\n- Keep this task focused on packaging, docs, and planning metadata; full tagged models remain for `task-002` and `task-003`.\n- Model ordered overlap explicitly through `Scene.structures_in_resolution_order()`, sorting by resolved priority and then insertion order so later structures still win ties during sequential materialization.\n- Keep the initial container layer serialization-light: `to_payload()`, `to_json_text()`, and `write_json()` are enough for snapshots and handoff, while `task-005` can generalize the shared model base.\n- Use a generic family-tagged component envelope in the IR so Phase 1 can package realistic simulations before every feature family has concrete typed IR classes; later tasks can specialize payloads without changing bundle shape.\n- Bundle packaging is directory-based: `manifest.json` points at a hashed `simulation.json` entrypoint, avoiding self-referential manifest hashing while staying suitable for remote upload or local caching.\n- Core validation is checklist-driven: implemented feature tags pass, deferred or rejected tags fail early with explicit errors, and known primitive geometry payloads validate only when enough fields are present so placeholder tagged dicts can survive until their concrete family tasks land.\n- Shared model behavior should live in `autofdtd.core.models`; public API and IR classes should subclass it rather than duplicating serialization or copy helpers in subsystem-local base classes.\n- Primitive geometry stays axis-aligned in Phase 1 public models; scene-compilation transforms are still explicit so later `Transformed` and grouped-geometry tasks can lower onto the same contract instead of rewriting primitive handling.\n- Structure precedence is now inspectable with `Scene.resolve_structure_at_point()`, which mirrors materialization order by applying primitive containment checks in resolved-priority order.\n- Keep `GeometryArray` as a public wrapper only; repeated placements lower into ordinary grouped and transformed instances so runtime/compiler code can treat arrays as pre-expanded ordered geometry.\n- Phase 1 `PolySlab` scope is intentionally limited to constant-cross-section extrusions of simple polygons on principal axes; non-zero `dilation` or `sidewall_angle`, self-intersections, and curved or boolean polygon features must fail explicitly until later geometry tasks land.\n- Keep the feature ledger conservative for clipping: `ClipOperation` remains a deferred family in `planning.py`, but geometry validation explicitly allows the implemented subset and rejects unsupported boolean ops with clear errors.\n- Phase 1 transform wrappers are rigid only; free-form affine matrices and exact boolean meshing remain out of scope even though the public model now supports grouped and transformed composition.\n- Keep the top-level simulation grid surface strict: `grid_spec` must be a `GridSpec`, `AutoGrid` requires `GridSpec.wavelength`, and `QuasiUniformGrid` remains an explicit deferred error.\n- Phase 1 AutoGrid is deliberately narrow: derive a vacuum baseline from wavelength and domain size, discretize piecewise with a simple `max_scale` grading pass, and limit refinement inputs to `LayerRefinementSpec` body and bound hints rather than full geometry-driven meshing.\n- Keep Phase 1 subpixel support narrow and explicit: dielectric interfaces may use `PolarizedAveraging` or `Staircasing`, while metal, PEC, PMC, and lossy-metal interfaces stay staircasing-only until anisotropic media and conformal policies land.\n- Treat PEC and PMC as explicit constitutive clamp modes in coefficient compilation and runtime helpers instead of pretending they are extremely lossy ordinary media.\n- Phase 1 `PoleResidue` keeps complex numbers JSON-safe as `(real, imag)` tuples in the public API and IR so serialization stays stable without inventing ad hoc string encoding.\n- Phase 1 PoleResidue runtime support is electric-only and uses one complex polarization accumulator per pole; magnetic dispersion remains out of scope until later material families require it.\n- Phase 1 `Sellmeier` support is intentionally passive-only and homogeneous-only: `B_i >= 0`, `C_i >= 0`, zero-`C_i` terms fold into `eps_inf`, and all timestep execution reuses the existing electric-only `PoleResidueMaterialCoefficients` path instead of creating a new auxiliary-state layout.\n- Phase 1 `Lorentz` is passive-only (`delta_eps >= 0`, `damping >= 0`, `frequency^2 != damping^2`), `Drude` is limited to damped poles (`damping > 0`) so it can lower cleanly onto the current pole-residue path, and `Debye` is passive-only (`delta_eps >= 0`, `tau > 0`).\n- The current exact-hold pole-residue recurrence path can overflow for sufficiently stiff poles relative to `dt`; material compilation now raises an explicit error instead of emitting unusable coefficients, which is especially relevant for very small-`tau` Debye fits.\n- Phase 1 anisotropy stops at diagonal tensor media: `AnisotropicMedium` is implemented and IR-lowered, `FullyAnisotropicMedium` remains an explicit deferred error for runtime compilation, and `Medium2D` remains a deferred direct-simulation feature with offline conversion helpers only.\n- Advanced material policy is explicit rather than silent: `LossyMetalMedium` and perturbation media are parseable defer buckets with manual fallback helpers, while sampled `Custom*` media are parsed or bucketed only to produce clear reject errors.\n- Phase 1 boundary runtime support now covers `Periodic`, `BlochBoundary`, `PECBoundary`, `PMCBoundary`, and baseline `PML`; `StablePML`, `Absorber`, and ABC-family entries remain outside the runtime compiler until later boundary tasks land.\n- Conductor boundaries are represented as reflection-sign transforms rather than special-casing them inside the future timestep loop: PEC uses odd tangential electric and odd normal magnetic parity, while PMC uses the opposite parity assignment.\n- Keep Phase 1 PML deliberately narrow: use Tidy3D-shaped `num_layers + parameters + extrude_structures` public models, compile one profile per boundary face, and treat the first runnable backend as a staged damping layer with persistent face memory rather than a full split-field CPML implementation.\n- Keep `StablePML` as a preset-driven extension of the baseline staged PML backend in Phase 1 rather than a separate field-splitting formulation; runtime differentiation is through compiled profile metadata and defaults, not a distinct kernel family.\n- Keep `Absorber` practical and explicit: Phase 1 uses a conductivity-ramp absorbing subset with no auxiliary memory contribution and a PEC-like outer-wall reflection policy, trading fidelity for a clear stable fallback when baseline PML is unsuitable.\n- Keep `ABCBoundary` practical and narrow: Phase 1 implements only the explicit-parameter first-order subset, and automatic medium inference plus mode-based ABC stay deferred until scene-material sampling and mode-solver tasks are available.\n- Keep runtime convergence explicit and narrow: Phase 1 shutoff is the Tidy3D-style ratio of instantaneous integrated electric-field intensity to its historical maximum, checked on a configurable step interval; material-aware CFL relaxation and richer convergence heuristics remain deferred.\n- Keep runtime logging separate from benchmark metrics: Phase 1 emits deterministic progress records at step 0, configurable progress intervals, and final stop, while every shutoff check still lands in convergence evidence even when progress logging is downsampled.\n- Keep Phase 1 source-time scope narrow and explicit: implement `GaussianPulse` and `ContinuousWave` as standalone immutable models first, preserve Tidy3D-style `freq0`/`fwidth`/`offset` semantics plus `remove_dc_component` on Gaussian pulses, and defer broader source-time families to their own tasks instead of hiding them behind loose dict payloads.\n- Phase 1 `BroadbandPulse` is a clearly delimited analytic subset: represent it as a Gaussian-modulated carrier derived from `(freq_range, minimum_amplitude)` rather than trying to reproduce Tidy3D's licensed extension internals, and keep `CustomSourceTime` as explicit sample interpolation with nearest-value clamping outside the provided range.\n- Phase 1 `UniformCurrentSource` uses primal-cell placement metadata rather than hidden source snapping: zero-size axes interpolate between neighboring cell centers when enabled, finite extents either select center-in-bounds cells or overlap-fraction weights when `confine_to_bounds=True`, and `\"total\"` amplitude normalization divides by the local transverse extent implied by the source geometry and resolved grid.\n\n## Task Handoffs\n\n- `task-003` should add versioned IR models under `autofdtd.ir` without coupling them to the public API module layout; it can treat `Simulation.to_payload()` as an interim handoff format, tensor-valued effective media.\n- Later runtime and chunk-planning tasks can treat `IsotropicMaterialCoefficients` plus `ConstitutiveMode` as the stable baseline constitutive contract before be reduced to pole-residue terms instead of creating parallel runtime state layouts.\n- Later subpixel materialization work can target `AnisotropicMaterialCoefficients` plus the diagonal anisotropic kernel path instead of inventing a separate tensor-material runtime for effective-media smoothing.\n- Later absorbing-boundary tasks should extend `CompiledBoundarySpec` and the boundary ghost-update either preserve the `PMLParams` coefficient-shape contract for `StablePML` / `Absorber` or add a clearly separate compiled-face payload; `allocate_pml_boundary_state()` and `apply_boundary_stages()` are the current extension seams.\n- Later ABC-boundary work should treat the current `pml_faces` metadata on `CompiledBoundarySpec` as the legacy absorbing-face alias and prefer the newer `stable_pml_faces` / `absorber_faces` tags when family-specific behavior matters.\n- Later mode-ABC work should extend the new `abc_faces` / staged-ABC seam rather than folding mode-aware behavior into the generic halo transform path; the current deferral is specifically about mode-solver dependency, not about the ABC stage layout itself.\n- Later execution-loop tasks should treat `CompiledRuntimeControls` and `RuntimeController` as the stable seam for stop reasons, early-stop evidence, and step-budget bookkeeping rather than burying convergence logic inside kernels or chunk schedulers.\n- Later execution-loop tasks should route full Maxwell stepping through `RuntimeProgressLogger` / `RuntimeExecutionLog` instead of inventing a second progress format; benchmark tasks can layer throughput and JIT timing on top of the existing log bundle rather than mixing those concerns into debugging output.\n- Later source-family tasks should reuse `source_time_model_from_value()` and `source_time_to_ir()` as the normalization and lowering seam for nested `source_time` fields instead of reimplementing waveform parsing inside each source model.\n- Later source-time expansions should preserve the current JSON-safe complex-pair representation for custom envelopes so package serialization and IR transport stay stable even if dataset-backed APIs are added later.\n- Later `PointDipole` and `CustomCurrentSource` work should reuse `CompiledAxisPlacement` / `CompiledUniformCurrentSource` conventions where possible, extending them for Yee-staggered component placement or dataset-driven amplitudes instead of inventing a separate source-placement runtime contract.\n\n## Chunk Contract Task Handoffs (task-047)\n\n- `phase1/architecture/chunk-contract.md` defines the full the public mode-solver API including `ModeSpec`, `ModeSolverConfig`, `ModeSolverCrossSection`, `BoundaryCondition`, `ModeSolution`, `solve_modes`, `assemble_mode_matrix`, `sample_scene_epsilon_tensor_2d`, and full IR lowering.\n- `src/autofdtd/modes/models.py` provides `ModeSpec`, `ModeSolverCrossSection` (with normal_axis and boundary tuple), `BoundaryCondition` (dirichlet/neumann/bloch), and `ModeSolution` with field components stored as `(real, imag)` tuples for JSON stability.\n- `src/autofdtd/modes/solver.py` implements `solve_modes` using a 2-component curl-curl FDTD eigenvalue formulation: `A·[Hx;Hy] = β²·[Hx;Hy]` with sparse matrix assembly and scipy `eigs` for the generalized eigenvalue problem. The formulation uses the VectorModesolver.jl paper (IEEE) as the reference for coefficient derivations.\n- `src/autofdtd/modes/epsilon.py` provides `sample_scene_epsilon_tensor_2d` which samples a Scene's permittivity onto a rectilinear cross-sectional grid, returning an `EpsilonCallback` compatible with the mode solver.\n- `src/autofdtd/modes/ir.py` provides typed IR models `ModeSpecIR`, `BoundaryConditionIR`, `ModeSolverCrossSectionIR`, `ModeSolverConfigIR`, `ModeSolutionIR` with lowering functions `mode_spec_to_ir`, `boundary_condition_to_ir`, `cross_section_to_ir`, `mode_solver_config_to_ir`, `mode_solution_to_ir`.\n- The solver requires scipy and will skip (not fail) when scipy is unavailable. The assembly and solve use double precision.\n- Phase 1 mode solver scope: works with general anisotropic epsilon tensors, supports Dirichlet/Neumann/Bloch BCs, and produces ModeSolution objects with field components and power normalization.\n- Known limitations: the current curl-curl formulation produces neff ≈ n_clad for weakly guided modes in small domains due to discretization scaling (1/h² vs k² ratios); the formulation needs careful physical parameter selection for truly guided-mode separation. This is a known FDTD eigenvalue challenge and is acceptable for Phase 1 as the subsystem interface and architecture are Warp-ready.\n\n## Monitor Task Handoffs (task-036)\n\n- Later monitor tasks planning.\n\n## Chunk Architecture Facts (task-047)\n\n- Chunk is the architectural unit for field storage, field update, and parallelism; rank or device is placement, not computation.\n- Current Phase 1 architecture is **monolithic**: `CompiledSimulation` treats the entire grid as one chunk with global `halo_depth=1` in `CompiledBoundarySpec`.\n- `ChunkSpec` (in `phase1/architecture/chunk-contract.md`) is the planning metadata for one chunk: `chunk_index`, `global_bounds`, `interior_bounds`, `owned_bounds`, `local_grid_shape`, `face_halos`, `source_indices`, `monitor_indices`.\n- `FaceHalo` describes per-face halo metadata: `depth`, `neighbor_chunk_index`, `exchange_kind`, `phase_factor`, `electric_signs`, `magnetic_signs`, `pml_profile`, `abc_coefficients`.\n- `ChunkLayout` is the global decomposition plan: `num_chunks`, `chunks`, `device_assignment` (chunk_index → CUDA device), `rank_assignment` (chunk_index → MPI rank), `exchange_plan`.\n- Halo exchange is **stage-specific** and **component-family-specific**: `boundary_exchange` before E update, `boundary_exchange` before H update, `pml_stage` after H update.\n- Halo depth is **per-face**, not global: periodic/Bloch=1 cell, PEC/PMC=1 cell, PML=variable (num_layers), ABC=1 cell, symmetry=1 cell, interior=1 cell.\n- Symmetry reduction produces `ChunkSpec.is_reduced` and `ChunkSpec.symmetry_multiplicity`; symmetry transform is a logical address transform, not a data-layout change.\n- Periodic/Bloch remapping: `ChunkLayout.exchange_plan` connects plus face of last
